story_type: crewed lunar flyby sets the human distance record
hook: The farthest any humans have ever traveled from Earth.
narration: Four astronauts flew farther from Earth than any humans ever.
They launched on April 1, 2026, the first crew sent toward the Moon in over fifty years.
Then came the burn that sent them out of Earth orbit and on toward the Moon.
Their path used the Moon's gravity to swing the capsule around and aim it back home.
Mission control told them they were now closer to the Moon than to Earth.
At their farthest, they were two hundred fifty-two thousand, seven hundred fifty-six miles from home.
outcome: After nearly ten days in space, the crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean.
title: Farther than any humans have gone
description:
NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover and Christina Koch and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen launched on Artemis II on April 1, 2026, flew around the Moon 252,756 miles from Earth, farther than any humans before them, and splashed down in the Pacific on April 10.
